meta.name: Agent Policy Index
meta.method: Every entry comes from a real contribution campaign run in October 2026: issues claimed, PRs opened, bots and policies met face to face, plus Greenlight friction measurements. Policy classes marked 'detected' were found by automated scans; classes marked 'verified' were confirmed by a policy file read or by direct campaign contact.

classes.label: Agent contributions banned
classes.meaning: The repo's agent policy forbids autonomous agent contributions and AI-drafted PR text. Do not submit there with an agent.

classes.label: AI disclosure required
classes.meaning: Agents may contribute, but the repo requires AI involvement to be disclosed in titles, bodies, and release notes.

classes.label: Assignment required
classes.meaning: You must be assigned the issue by a maintainer before work counts. Unassigned PRs may be auto-closed.

classes.label: Claim first
classes.meaning: Comment on the issue to claim it before you start. Silent starts lose races.

classes.label: Triage hold
classes.meaning: Issues in triage are not ready to build on. Wait until the triage labels clear.

classes.label: Outside PRs paused
classes.meaning: The repo has structurally paused or auto-closes external pull requests. Do not target it.

classes.label: Maintainer-only PRs
classes.meaning: External PRs are not accepted. The contribution is a detailed, verified issue comment.

classes.label: Collaborators-only PRs
classes.meaning: Only collaborators can open PRs. Outside fork-based PRs are rejected or never land.

classes.label: Vouch required
classes.meaning: A maintainer must vouch for you (or you must join a contributor list) before your PR survives.

classes.label: CLA required
classes.meaning: A Contributor License Agreement signature is required before merge. Find the exact path, it is fragmented across repos.

classes.label: DCO sign-off required
classes.meaning: Every commit needs a Signed-off-by trailer. Unsigned commits fail the gate.

classes.label: Discussion first
classes.meaning: Open an issue or discussion and get agreement before you build, especially for new features.

classes.label: Bot-gated intake
classes.meaning: A bot triages incoming work with labels like needs-product-decision. Claims are fine; PRs wait for a human signal.

classes.label: Open to agent-assisted PRs
classes.meaning: No structural gate found against agent-assisted contributions. Standard contribution rules still apply.

entries.headline: Autonomous agents may not contribute, and AI may not draft PR text.
entries.what_to_do: Read their AGENTS.md on main before anything. If you are a human who understands the fix, you may open the PR yourself with a disclosure; an agent must not post the PR, its text, or any comment.
entries.evidence: AGENTS.md verified on main (2026-10-17): contributions may only be submitted by a human who understands them; agents may not draft or post PR titles, descriptions, issues, or comments. Our agent-posted protocol claim comment on issue #36626 was deleted the same day once the policy was found; the one-line fix was built and pushed to a fork and is awaiting a manual open by the contributor.
entries.our_record: Fix built and pushed to a fork branch; PR not opened by us per the ban

entries.headline: Autonomous agent contributions are not allowed, and AI-generated maintainer comments may be hidden.
entries.what_to_do: You may use AI as a coding tool, but a human must own the work, write the comments in their own words, and disclose any AI context in quote blocks. Do not submit anything an agent produced on its own.
entries.evidence: astral-sh/.github/AI_POLICY.md (read 2026-10-17): AI should not be used to generate comments when communicating with maintainers; we do not allow autonomous agents to be used for contributing; pull requests believed autonomous will be closed. Never targeted by the campaign; added as an exclusion after the policy read.
entries.our_record: Never targeted: agent ban found before any claim

entries.headline: Unsolicited outside PRs are paused and a workflow closes them within about a minute.
entries.what_to_do: Do not claim, build, or open. The policy names AI-generated PR volume as the cause.
entries.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md states pull requests from outside the core team are paused; the 'Close external PRs' workflow auto-closed both of our PRs (#16580, #16581) despite clean claims and passing builds. Friction Index detection quotes the pause language. Learned the campaign's standing vetting rule: read CONTRIBUTING and the workflow list before claiming.
entries.our_record: 2 PRs closed unmerged (#16580, #16581)

entries.headline: External PRs are paused, explicitly citing AI coding agent PR volume.
entries.what_to_do: Do not target. Same structural class as activepieces; the pause is the gate, not any single issue.
entries.evidence: CONTRIBUTING states pull requests from outside the maintainer team are paused. Found by scout B on 2026-10-17 before any claim was posted; never targeted.
entries.our_record: Never targeted: pause found before any claim

entries.headline: Issues are welcome; pull requests are not accepted from outside.
entries.what_to_do: Do not open a PR. The contribution is a detailed issue comment: reproduction, root cause, and a fix sketch.
entries.evidence: Repo policy: 'We accept issues, not pull requests. Design and implementation are done by the maintainers.' We posted a verified comment (repro plus fix sketch) on issue #2723 on 2026-10-15; no reply yet. Friction Index detection quotes the policy language.
entries.our_record: 1 verified issue comment (#2723)

entries.headline: Issues are welcome; pull requests are not accepted from outside.
entries.what_to_do: Same class as inspector: contribute via detailed issue comments. The policy even asks for the prompt behind a local fix.
entries.evidence: Repo policy mirrors inspector ('We accept issues, not pull requests'). We posted a verified comment on issue #5153 on 2026-10-15; no reply yet. Friction Index detection quotes the policy language.
entries.our_record: 1 verified issue comment (#5153)

entries.headline: PR creation rejects non-collaborators; outside fork-based PRs effectively do not exist.
entries.what_to_do: Do not claim or build. Two of our claims (#4576, #4707) are dead ends here; PR creation 404s for outsiders.
entries.evidence: Scale-wave discovery (2026-10-17): PR creation 404s for non-collaborators and zero fork-based PRs appeared in the last 100 closed PRs. Note: the repo-intel row previously recorded 'maintainers merge externals'; the newer, stronger evidence is that outsiders cannot open PRs at all. Claims #4576 and #4707 were posted before this was found and are queued for release.
entries.our_record: 2 claims posted (#4576, #4707); both dead on the gate

entries.headline: You must be on the .github/VOUCHED.td contributor list, and an accepted-label is required before your PR.
entries.what_to_do: Skip unless a maintainer vouches for you. Not on the vouch list means no PR, structurally. Note: our repo-intel row recorded no CLA, but the policy docs describe a CLA signing step, so verify the exact signing path at PR time.
entries.evidence: Policy docs: unvouched authors get a comment that nothing is built from outside; docs also describe a CLA signature step and an open-an-issue-first rule (Friction Index detection quotes all three). Never targeted after the gate was found.
entries.our_record: 0 (passed: vouch gate)

entries.headline: A maintainer vouch is required before your first PR; unvouched PRs are auto-closed.
entries.what_to_do: Do not open a PR. The vouch is requested via a dedicated discussion/issue flow (discussion #5010).
entries.evidence: Scale-wave discovery (2026-10-17): vouch-check-pr.yml auto-closes PRs from authors without a maintainer vouch; discussion #5010 documents the vouch request path. Friction Index detection (hand-verified 2026-10-13) records the same gate. Never targeted after the gate was found.
entries.our_record: 0 (ineligible until vouched)

entries.headline: You must be assigned the issue before your work counts; the issue-link check fails until then.
entries.what_to_do: Comment to request assignment and wait. Do not apply labels manually, and follow the strict PR body format (prose plus a code example).
entries.evidence: Our PR #5757 (2026-10-15) sat waiting on assignment; it is now maintainer-approved and awaiting merge. The repo's check-issue-link bot enforces the link.
entries.our_record: 1 PR open (#5757, maintainer-approved)

entries.headline: PRs not linked to a maintainer-assigned issue are closed automatically.
entries.what_to_do: Do not post a PR unless a maintainer assigned the linked issue to you. 'Do not have an agent post them' is the practical rule.
entries.evidence: Scale-wave discovery (2026-10-17): PRs not linked to maintainer-assigned issues are auto-closed. Friction Index detection (hand-verified 2026-10-13) records the assignment culture across the MCP SDKs. Ineligible until assigned.
entries.our_record: 0 (ineligible until assigned)

entries.headline: You comment to claim and wait for a maintainer to assign you; the claim alone is not enough.
entries.what_to_do: Comment and wait; do not build until the assignment lands. Note the payout amounts in its Stellar Wave bounty program are undocumented (terms page 404).
entries.evidence: Repo uses an orderly claim queue (three claimants on day one, no assignments yet on 2026-10-15). Our assignment request on #1361 is still pending. Conventional Commits required; npm run ci must be green.
entries.our_record: Assignment requested on #1361, still pending

entries.headline: Comment to claim before you start, and sign every commit with DCO.
entries.what_to_do: Claim in the same pass you spot the issue; races here are fast. Every commit needs the Signed-off-by trailer.
entries.evidence: Repo policy: 'Do not claim an issue silently. Comment before starting work, and check the thread first' plus the DCO requirement (Friction Index detection quotes both). Claims land within hours in this repo.
entries.our_record: 6 PRs open; human reviews pending

entries.headline: Claim first, sign every commit, and ship one .changes file per PR.
entries.what_to_do: Read AGENTS.md before building; pnpm verify is the real gate. Never edit CHANGELOG yourself; red-test-first proof belongs in the PR.
entries.evidence: House rules live in AGENTS.md; CI flakes on the Windows install gate are not your bug. Our PR #1726 merged 85 minutes after opening on 2026-10-17 (maintainer divshekhar engages on PR questions).
entries.our_record: 6 PRs opened, 1 merged (#1726)

entries.headline: The maintainer asks you to comment to claim before starting; otherwise the repo is open.
entries.what_to_do: Claim first, then build. Small maintainer repos merge fast, so keep the PR tight.
entries.evidence: Hand-verified 2026-10-14: maintainer asks contributors to comment to claim before starting (Friction Index detection records it). Our PR #91 merged.
entries.our_record: 1 PR merged (#91)

entries.headline: Agents are welcome, with full AI disclosure: [AI] prefixes, disclosure in the PR body, and a plain-language release note.
entries.what_to_do: Prefix agent PR titles and commits with [AI], disclose AI use in the PR description, and add a release note file under upcoming-release-notes/ written for non-technical humans (enforced in review). Expect 2 approving reviews.
entries.evidence: AGENTS.md policy read 2026-10-17: open to anyone, no CLA, no assignment gate; disclosure and release-note rules were enforced on our PR #9240 in review. Friction: 57 percent outside merge share, 1.5 day median. Two of our PRs were closed unmerged on 2026-10-17 (#9240 by matt-fidd after full review rounds, #9250 silently by a maintainer).
entries.our_record: 2 PRs opened (#9240, #9250), both closed unmerged

entries.headline: The open pool is feature requests stuck in status: needs triage. Do not build until triage clears.
entries.what_to_do: Watch, do not build. Re-scan in a week; triage-held issues are the class Greenlight's triage-hold gate was built for.
entries.evidence: Scouted 2026-10-15: open pool was feature requests marked needs-triage with no good-first-issues; skipped this round. Merges outsiders normally once issues clear.
entries.our_record: 0 (skipped: triage pool)

entries.headline: A real CLA signature is required, through n8n's own CLA bot, and a comment signature alone does not satisfy it.
entries.what_to_do: Sign at the bot's link (cla-bot-prod.users.n8n.cloud via GitHub OAuth), then post /cla-check on the PR. Also: every issue is mirrored to Linear, so check duplicates before building.
entries.evidence: Our PR #41235 went through the custom CLA path (cla-signed label, 2026-10-16); comment-only signatures fail here. n8n-assistant bot and cubic-dev-ai review actively.
entries.our_record: 1 PR open (#41235, CLA signed)

entries.headline: Marimo's own CLA must be signed at PR time; PRs fail until you sign.
entries.what_to_do: Sign at marimo.io/cla when you open. For substantial UI changes, get maintainer approval before building (approval-gated by policy).
entries.evidence: Policy: all new PRs fail until the CLA is signed by leaving a comment. Our draft PR #11270 and closed-unmerged #11271 (maintainer closed the underlying issue) are in flight; an approval ask on #11244 is pending.
entries.our_record: 1 draft PR (#11270), 1 closed unmerged (#11271), approval ask pending

entries.headline: CLA agreement via cla-assistant is required before merge.
entries.what_to_do: Sign through cla-assistant when the bot asks. Note that soft claims age out here, so an old claim with no PR may be re-claimable (carefully).
entries.evidence: cla-assistant.io/langfuse/langfuse is the signing path (Friction Index detection quotes it). Our backup target #18053 had a soft claim from 2026-09-30 with no PR by 2026-10-15.
entries.our_record: 0 (backup target identified)

entries.headline: ClawSweeper labels incoming work: no-new-fix-pr, needs-maintainer-review, needs-product-decision.
entries.what_to_do: Claiming is fine, but build locally and park the PR until a maintainer gives scope confirmation.
entries.evidence: Claim posted 2026-10-14 with no maintainer reply since; the build sits verified on a fork (1 commit) behind a no-new-fix-pr style gate. Claim-and-wait is the pattern here.
entries.our_record: Build parked on fork; PR opens on maintainer signal

entries.headline: Reproduce first, then build. Review is fast and high quality.
entries.what_to_do: Check for competing PRs before you start; first claim wins socially here. Vercel deploy authorization on previews is maintainer-side, not your failure.
entries.evidence: cubic-dev-ai reviewed within hours on our PRs (2026-10-14). Two of our PRs are open (#5141 cubic-approved, #5164).

entries.headline: No formal gates; the trap is needs-repro issues that do not reproduce on current source.
entries.what_to_do: Reproduce on the current release before building. Issue #18708 existed only in the published 3.90.2 tarball, not in source or 3.91.0, so no honest fix was possible there.
entries.evidence: Two of our PRs are open on main (#18820, #18821), both survived CodeRabbit rounds. One claim was withdrawn honestly after the needs-repro check failed.

entries.headline: No formal gates; the race trap is maintainer-assigned issues with open PRs you cannot see from list views.
entries.what_to_do: Read the issue's comments before claiming. Inherited collection params and runner merge behavior are known-hard areas that pay off.
entries.evidence: Our candidate #9511 turned out maintainer-assigned with an open PR (2026-10-15). Three of our PRs are open (#9556, #9561, #9562), all surviving CodeRabbit review rounds.

entries.headline: No formal gates; issues are precise and file-named. Note the repo was renamed from get-convex/convex-js.
entries.what_to_do: Claim and build. Hiring signal: Convex is hiring in SF on strong revenue growth, so the repo rewards fast, clean PRs.
entries.evidence: Three of our PRs are open (#203, #204, #205), including two from the 2026-10-17 wave. GitHub search still 422s on the old get-convex owner; REST redirects.

entries.headline: Title lint is the only automation: PR titles must be conventional commits. Otherwise open, but races are same-day.
entries.what_to_do: Move fast and claim in the same pass you spot the issue. Soft claims can sit invisible for days (we missed #23757), so timeline cross-references are mandatory.
entries.evidence: Our PR #23808 is open (one-line EISDIR fix, red-test-first). Friction: 47 percent outside merge share, 1.7 day median. Same-day races are the norm.
entries.our_record: 1 PR open (#23808)

entries.headline: Open, but the org triage bot races you: it opens draft fix PRs on fresh issues.
entries.what_to_do: Claim the moment an issue passes vetting. Include a changeset; the changeset bot confirms it.
entries.evidence: Our PR #17489 is open (one-line trailing-slash fix plus changeset). The svelte-triage-bot opened a draft fix PR on neighboring issue #17466 while we worked. Friction: 83 percent outside merge share.
entries.our_record: 1 PR open (#17489)

entries.headline: No formal gates; long-lived feature requests are a claim graveyard of serial claims that never land.
entries.what_to_do: Pick tightly-scoped bugs over feature requests. Action-required workflow conclusions mean 'waiting on maintainer approval', not a failure.
entries.evidence: Our PR #8757 is open (ingredient duplication fix, head verified); #8753 was closed unmerged silently by the repo owner on 2026-10-17. Friction: 83 percent outside merge share, 6.6 day median.
entries.our_record: 1 PR open (#8757), 1 closed unmerged (#8753)

entries.headline: No formal gates; assignment asks can sit unanswered for over a year, so just build.
entries.what_to_do: Do not wait for assignment; open the PR. The weak-pr-mention flag earned its keep here (an issue that mentions a fix without making one).
entries.evidence: Two of our PRs are open (#8218, #8219) from the 2026-10-17 wave. Friction: 7 percent outside merge share, 0.5 day median.

entries.headline: No formal gates; merges outside work readily and steadily.
entries.what_to_do: A reliable steady-progress lane: keep PRs small and conventional.
entries.evidence: Three of our PRs merged (#180, #181, #191) starting 2026-10-08.

entries.headline: No formal gates observed; early days for us here.
entries.what_to_do: Claim and build; no replies yet, so set expectations on review speed accordingly.
entries.evidence: Two of our PRs are open (#1797, #1798) with checks green; no reviews yet as of 2026-10-15.

entries.headline: No formal gates observed; early days for us here.
entries.what_to_do: Claim and build; checks are green on our PR, reviews pending.
entries.evidence: Our PR #4631 is open and green with no reviews yet as of 2026-10-15.
entries.our_record: 1 PR open (#4631)

entries.headline: No formal gates observed; early days for us here.
entries.what_to_do: Claim and build; no checks had run yet on our PR as of 2026-10-15.
entries.evidence: Our PR #14839 is open; no checks had run yet when last checked.
entries.our_record: 1 PR open (#14839)

entries.headline: No gates at all: no CONTRIBUTING, no AGENTS.md, no CLA, no auto-close automation.
entries.what_to_do: A clean, open lane. Claim and build with normal good practice.
entries.evidence: Wave discovery (2026-10-17): no policy files or automation found. Our PR #172 is open; no reply yet.
entries.our_record: 1 PR open (#172)

entries.headline: No formal gates, but same-day races are the norm.
entries.what_to_do: Claim in the same pass you spot the issue. List views lie about comments; read the thread.
entries.evidence: Issue #9611 was claimed 2026-10-14 by another contributor hours before our vetting pass (2026-10-15); we passed. Friction: 37 percent outside merge share.
entries.our_record: 0 (raced: claimed same-day by another contributor)

entries.headline: No formal gates, but the company's own bot claims hot issues within hours.
entries.what_to_do: Scout the fallback pool, not the hot issues. A claim from the company bot is a social claim that wins.
entries.evidence: Observed 2026-10-15: posthog[bot] opens its own PRs on hot issues within hours of filing. Skipped this round.
entries.our_record: 0 (skipped: company bot races)

entries.headline: No assignment gate in practice: small, well-scoped PRs get reviewed fast.
entries.what_to_do: Open the PR; disclosure-only AI rules apply (deno-class). Note: an earlier friction measurement recorded an assignment culture, but our PR #3044 (2026-10-17) moved without one; treat the earlier reading as superseded.
entries.evidence: Our PR #3044 (v1.x requestId-0 backport) is open; the repo's own note is 'no assignment gate, small PRs get reviewed fast'. Friction Index detection still quotes older 'discuss before you code' language for new features, so open a discussion first for significant changes.
entries.our_record: 1 PR open (#3044)

entries.headline: Disclosure-only AI rule; otherwise open with serious review standards.
entries.what_to_do: Disclose AI assistance; expect real technical review. Benchmark claims against real behavior (we diffed deepEqual against real Node).
entries.evidence: Our PR #37038 (node:assert deepEqual symmetry, 13 of 14 vs real Node with the divergence documented) is open. Repo expects agent contributors to disclose.
entries.our_record: 1 PR open (#37038)

entries.headline: A PR-speed repo: contributors open fix PRs without claiming, and maintainers engage same-day.
entries.what_to_do: Do not rely on comment checks. Walk the issue timeline for cross-referenced PRs before calling anything unclaimed.
entries.evidence: Two claims posted 2026-10-15; the race on #1988 taught the mandatory timeline cross-reference check (the 'race' PR had closed unmerged 17 hours before the scout). Friction Index detection quotes the discuss-first guidance from CONTRIBUTING.
entries.our_record: 2 claims posted

entries.headline: High issue velocity; open an issue and get maintainer agreement before building new providers.
entries.what_to_do: Check assignees first: some issues are pre-assigned to staff. Some repos in this ecosystem are closed backends, so verify the fix lives in the repo before building.
entries.evidence: Two claims posted 2026-10-15; races in the high-velocity pool were observed on the 2026-10-17 wave. Friction Index detection quotes the maintainer-agreement guidance.
entries.our_record: 2 claims posted

entries.headline: No formal gates; merges outsiders the same day.
entries.what_to_do: Claim within hours of filing. Fresh issues are the whole game here.
entries.evidence: Observed 2026-10-15: 5 merges in one day, 2 verified external. Issue #1147 was claimed same-day by another contributor; we are watching.
entries.our_record: 0 (watching: same-day claims)

entries.headline: PRs must link an issue (ftc-require-issue workflow); buildable issues move in cohorts.
entries.what_to_do: Link the issue in the PR body. Claims here arrive in waves (a Stanford collaboration cohort claimed everything buildable on 2026-10-12), so revisit when fresh issues land.
entries.evidence: Skipped 2026-10-15: every buildable good-first-issue was claimed in a cohort. Our claim on #8246 was withdrawn with cause (the request was the author pitching their own commercial product).
entries.our_record: 0 (claim withdrawn with cause: #8246)

entries.headline: New features need a discussion first; bugs are a different lane.
entries.what_to_do: Open a discussion for features; for bugs, claim and build. Races were observed on three scouted issues on the 2026-10-17 wave.
entries.evidence: Friction Index detection quotes the discussion-first rule for new features. We scouted #51629, #51656, and #51545 on 2026-10-17 and found all raced; no claim was posted. Friction: 82 percent outside merge share.
entries.our_record: 0 (scouted: all three issues raced)

entries.headline: No claim requirement, no CLA, friendly. Umbrella issues span multiple repos.
entries.what_to_do: Check which repo owns the fix before claiming. Changing shipped output semantics needs maintainer sign-off first.
entries.evidence: Two of our PRs are open (#310 circuit-to-canvas, #858 circuit-to-svg); the Gerber-anchor fix is held for maintainer sign-off. Snapshot-heavy repos make pushes big, use the web upload path.

entries.headline: No formal gates, but same-day soft claims are the main hazard.
entries.what_to_do: Comment-level claims ('Working on this') land within hours and are easy to miss; the claim layer has to run on the standard path. Model and hardware issues dominate the tracker, and many are not sandbox-buildable.
entries.evidence: Issue #19078 was raced by a same-day 'Working on this' comment the pattern layer missed (2026-10-17); #19040 was unbuildable here. Friction: 54 percent outside merge share, 0.8 day median.
entries.our_record: 0 (raced: same-day soft claim on #19078)

entries.headline: LLM-generated PRs, descriptions, and comments are refused; LLM fixes for good-first-issues are closed automatically.
entries.what_to_do: Do not submit here with an agent and do not post anything LLM-generated: PRs, descriptions, comments, and reviews are all covered. A human writing everything themselves is a different matter; anything generated gets closed.
entries.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md (read 2026-10-17): 'We ask you not to open PRs generated with an LLM.' 'Posting descriptions or comments that have been generated by an LLM is not acceptable.' 'Using LLMs to fix issues labelled as good first issue is forbidden, and those PRs will be closed automatically.' Read-only evaluation; nothing claimed or posted.
entries.our_record: No claims or PRs posted (read-only policy evaluation)

entries.headline: Contributions from autonomous agents are not accepted and may be closed without notice.
entries.what_to_do: Do not submit an autonomous-agent PR; it may be closed without notice. A human in the loop using LLM coding assistance is welcomed by the policy, so the human must own and drive the submission.
entries.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md (read 2026-10-17): 'we don't accept contributions from autonomous agents. Pull requests that appear to violate this may be closed without notice.' The same section notes that LLM coding assistance with a human in the loop is welcomed. Read-only evaluation; nothing claimed or posted.
entries.our_record: No claims or PRs posted (read-only policy evaluation)

entries.headline: Autonomous agent contributions are not accepted under the Open Home Foundation AI policy.
entries.what_to_do: Do not submit an autonomous-agent PR. A human may use AI tools as an aid only if they fully understand and can explain every change submitted.
entries.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md (read 2026-10-17) adopts the Open Home Foundation AI Policy (AI_POLICY.md): 'AI tools are welcome as an aid, but you must fully understand and be able to explain every change you submit. Contributions made by autonomous agents are not accepted.' AGENTS.md repeats the autonomous-contribution ban. Read-only evaluation; nothing claimed or posted.
entries.our_record: No claims or PRs posted (read-only policy evaluation)

entries.headline: No LLM-generated content at all, in code or documentation.
entries.what_to_do: Do not submit anything containing LLM-generated content: code, docs, or text from tools like Copilot or ChatGPT. A human writing every word themselves is a different matter; the ban covers generated content.
entries.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md '# LLM/"AI" Contributions' (read 2026-10-17): 'Contributions must not include content generated by large language models or other probabilistic tools, including but not limited to Copilot or ChatGPT.' The policy covers code, documentation, and pull-request text. Read-only evaluation; nothing claimed or posted.
entries.our_record: No claims or PRs posted (read-only policy evaluation)

entries.headline: No generative-AI content anywhere in external contributions: code, tests, docs, PRs, or comments.
entries.what_to_do: Do not submit with an agent and do not post AI-generated text anywhere: PR descriptions, PR comments, issue descriptions, and issue comments are all covered. A human submitting fully human-written work is a different matter.
entries.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md '## Use of Generative AI Tools' (read 2026-10-17): 'We will not consider any content generated by generative AI tooling (GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) in external contributions, including: code, tests, documentation, PR descriptions, PR comments, issue descriptions, and issue comments.' Read-only evaluation; nothing claimed or posted.
entries.our_record: No claims or PRs posted (read-only policy evaluation)

entries.headline: Autonomous AI agents may not submit pull requests, and AI-generated comments are banned.
entries.what_to_do: Do not submit an autonomous-agent PR and do not post AI-generated comments; discussions are for humans only. A human contributing with AI assistance must disclose it in a commit trailer and fully understand the work.
entries.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md points to the org-level AI Contribution Policy (mastodon/.github AI_POLICY.md), read 2026-10-17: 'Autonomous AI agents may not submit Pull Requests to Mastodon repositories.' 'Do not post comments on issues or PRs that are AI-generated. Discussions on the Mastodon repositories are for humans only.' AI-assisted contributions require disclosure via a commit trailer plus full understanding. Read-only evaluation; nothing claimed or posted.
entries.our_record: No claims or PRs posted (read-only policy evaluation)

entries.headline: Autonomous agent contributions are banned via the org-wide AI policy linked from CONTRIBUTING.
entries.what_to_do: Same class as astral-sh/uv: a human must own the work and write the comments in their own words, and may not use an agent to contribute. Do not submit autonomous-agent PRs.
entries.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md (read 2026-10-17): 'We require all use of AI in contributions to follow our AI Policy,' with a link to astral-sh/.github/AI_POLICY.md, which states: 'We do not allow autonomous agents to be used for contributing to our projects. We will close any pull requests that we believe were made autonomously.' Same org policy as astral-sh/uv. Read-only evaluation; nothing claimed or posted.

entries.headline: No fully-autonomous AI agent submissions; AI-assisted coding with disclosure is welcome.
entries.what_to_do: Do not submit issues, PRs, or reviews from a fully autonomous agent. A human may use AI coding tools and must disclose the tool and how it was used in the PR description.
